Use the real structured edit tool. Return ONLY JSON {"edits":[{"node":"an actual node ID from the source catalogue","changes":{}}]}. No fences or prose. One to sixteen node edits; no whole files or whole functions.
Maintain owned-buffer transfer across the two files. touch(buf:buffer,x:u8)->buffer (Rust Vec<u8>) takes a nonempty zeroed owner, writes x XOR 90 to byte 0, and returns the SAME owner with unchanged length, no allocation or clone. entrypoint allocates one zeroed owner of length (a AND 7)+1, calls touch exactly once with that owner and low byte of b, reads the returned byte, releases every loan and owner, and returns byte+4096*length+256*(c AND 7). Keep both signatures. Both files need changes. At most one logical allocation; no live owners or loans on normal return.
The task's references to files mean their editable symbols; this interface accepts node edits only.
Every Rust edit uses changes:{"text":"complete replacement fragment"}. Rust replacements are complete expression or type fragments. Preserve unselected syntax; include explicit parentheses when needed to keep surrounding precedence. Parameter/return types are read-only unless policy is migrate.

Real rustc still decides whether the requested target conversion exists. Normal as casts remain available.
